conventions.convention: The torsion linking expression is (C·y)/n modulo Z, where ∂C=nx, with intersection signs determined by the orientation of the three-manifold.
A linking metabolizer satisfies P=P⊥; equivalently it is isotropic and |P|²=|A|. This is a finite linking-form condition, distinct from a primitive Seifert-lattice metabolizer.
PTFA uses a finite subnormal series: each subgroup need only be normal in the next. The trivial group uses the length-zero series.
Zero surgery fills the preferred longitude. In its q-fold cover, the free meridian generator is the closed lift of μ^q, and its free coordinate is ℓ/q.
Prime-power-order characters have order p^e with e≥1. An extension over a disk cover may have larger p-power order than the original character.
The Casson–Gordon class is the rationalized twisted-minus-ordinary nonsingular Witt-form difference divided by the bounding multiplicity. Its signature is the one-sided limit t=e^{iθ}, θ→0+.
The disk-band construction uses V_ij=lk(a_i^+,a_j) and a linear-first equivariant pairing with matrix (1-t)V+(1-t^{-1})Vᵀ. At t=1 the zero matrix is not a basis matrix for ordinary middle homology.
Von Neumann matrix traces are unnormalized. Algebraic harmonic projection modules embed densely into their Hilbert completions; this embedding need not be onto.

Topological gluing additivity concerns entire closed boundary components with supplied collars and one compatible coefficient system. Boundary intersection operators may have nonclosed range; bounded invertibility is asserted for closed manifolds.

The general group-signature theorem establishes independence among smooth bounds and injective target enlargements; it does not supply comparison with a nonsmooth TOP bound or an analytic eta definition.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. Let K be a smooth slice knot, let q be a prime power, let D be a smooth slice disk, and let P_D be the induced metabolizer in H₁(Σ_q(K);Z). For every prime-power-order character χ that vanishes on P_D, the Casson–Gordon signature defect σ(K,χ) is zero.

Assume AC. For a fixed prime-power cover degree and prime-power order character, the rationalized difference between the twisted and untwisted Casson–Gordon intersection-form Witt classes, divided by the bounding multiplicity r, is independent of the chosen multiple and bounding pair. It defines a class in W(C(t))⊗Q.

Assume AC. Let D⊂B⁴ be a smooth proper disk, let p be prime, and let q=p^k with k≥1. The q-fold cyclic cover W_{D,q} of B⁴ branched along D is a compact connected oriented 4-manifold with H_i(W_{D,q};Q)=0 for every i>0 and boundary Σ_q(∂D).

Assume AC. Let W be a compact connected smooth oriented 4-manifold with rational homology of a point and connected boundary Y. Then Y is a rational homology sphere, and P=ker(H₁(Y;Z)→H₁(W;Z)) is a metabolizer for the torsion linking form λ_Y.
For a smooth proper disk D, prime-power q, and prime-power-order boundary character χ, χ vanishes on P_D if and only if it extends to a character of prime-power order on H₁(W_{D,q};Z), assuming AC.

Under full AC, compact oriented collared topological manifolds with the specified regular coefficients have bounded finite-projective chain models, completed reduced cap duality and weak exactness. Ordinary and L² signatures add under compatible gluing along unions of entire closed boundary components.

Assume AC. Closed oriented smooth four-manifolds have equal ordinary and regular-coefficient L² signatures for every discrete target. Smooth bounding defects exist after injective target enlargement, are independent of those smooth bounding data, and are uniformly bounded for each fixed closed oriented smooth three-manifold.

Under AC, the supplied finite smooth disk-band Seifert data give an actual oriented zero-surgery bound W_F with meridional fundamental group Z, ordinary metabolic intersection form of dimension 2g, and nontrivial-character intersection matrices (1-z)V+(1-z^{-1})Vᵀ, including singular matrices.
Assume AC. For every smooth oriented knot K and q≥2, H₁(M_{0,q};Z)≅H₁(Σ_q(K);Z)⊕Z, where the free summand is generated by the closed lift of μ^q.

In ZF, an explicitly supplied finite-free chain domination of a nonnegative right-module chain complex yields an explicitly constructed bounded finite-projective chain-homotopy equivalent complex; its lower terms may be finite free and its top term is an explicit idempotent image.

alerts.finding: The Statement instructs: “do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face.” Proof 3.1 nevertheless asserts: “a positive meridian moves through the q sheets cyclically”. For the literal cut-sheet construction, leaving that seam unglued leaves banks at which continuation from the last sheet to the first is unavailable; in a normal disk this does not give the asserted cyclic local model w↦w^q. Proof 1.1 and the schematic describe a chain of q−1 seams, but supply no additional identification or handle-cancellation equivalence reconciling that chain with the cyclic covering map. The standard surgery-matrix conclusion may hold, but the explicitly stated construction and its claimed covering property need owning-batch adjudication. This supplier is used by both assigned examples for the double-cover surgery presentation.

seams_checked.note: Positive-meridian covers, longitude filling, the root-product criterion and the double-cover matrix are cited with their stated conventions. The separate alert concerns the surgery supplier's own construction, rather than an overstatement by this batch.

The positive-push Hermitian matrix agrees. Canonical finite-cyclic calculations explicitly use actual matrix inertia, including singular matrices; they do not substitute the prerequisite's averaged knot-signature value at an Alexander root.
The obstruction and disk constructions retain smooth proper disks and full AC. The square-knot example uses the smooth reverse-mirror ribbon result under the stronger full-choice hypothesis.
Finite linking metabolizers are defined separately from primitive Seifert-lattice metabolizers. No algebraic concordance conclusion is used as a substitute for a disk-induced linking metabolizer.

The finite twisted-chain and coefficient conventions are used as context. Casson–Gordon boundary acyclicity and the cover-tensor identification are supplied by the separate explicit character-twist lemma, rather than inferred from a torsion definition.

The current direct use in Donaldson diagonalization is the ordinary-signature-zero conclusion for the full boundary of an actual compact oriented five-manifold. The consumer supplies a smooth bordism and retains full AC.

Citing Facts preserve the PTFA subnormal convention, supplied unitary structures, finite-projective versus finite-CW distinction, weak exactness, whole-component gluing and normalized finite-cyclic means. Smooth rho independence and uniformity are used in their smooth scope; TOP comparisons are expressly assigned to a separate external closed-TOP equality.
